- Default scrollbar thumbs get a thin contrast stroke so they read over same-coloured content (packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:; packages/blitz-paint/src/render.rs:); a test asserts default scrollbar thumbs carry a contrast stroke (tests/blitz-tests/tests/scrollbars.rs:)
- The harness holds one `VirtualClock` its documents share; `tick` and `advance_time` move it, and `screenshot`, `screenshot_rect`, `text_contrast` and `settle` never do.

| Loopback listeners (blitz-net unit tests) | no fixture file: `delivers_network_and_bad_url_errors` and `http_error_body_is_not_delivered_as_css`, in the crate's `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, each bind a `std::net::TcpListener` on `127.0.0.1:0`, test-only TCP on loopback, served by no binary and reached by no caller (arch §Occupied Resources); their stand-in handler is §8's | (packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-net/src/lib.rs:) |

- **`run {selection}`:** `stand` = one `--test {stem}` per `tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_*.rs` present · `all` = the whole package, no `--test` · `{name}` = one file, matching `^[a-z0-9_]+$` with `tests/blitz-tests/tests/{name}.rs` present; anything else exits 2. It runs `cargo test -p blitz-tests --locked [--test …]` with merged output to `run.log` (truncated at the run's start), sets `status.json`'s run state `running` then `passed` or `failed`, and parses libtest's pretty lines into events. The outcome is `passed` only when cargo exited 0, no test failed and at least one test line parsed — otherwise `failed`, exit 1: an empty run is never a pass. `run stand` with no `stand_*.rs` present is an empty run — no cargo call, `cargo_exit` null, exit 1 (scripts/agent-run.sh:; scripts/agent-run.sh:)

- **blitz-dom** — optional `tracing` logging, `println!` debug dumps and `debug_timer` phase timings (packages/blitz-dom/src/lib.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/debug.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:)

- A select list through the host and the role: `host_log` and `mcp_log` each hold a test that opens a select's list and chooses in it, through the host or the `mcp` role, with 0 option needles at `RUST_LOG=trace` (examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs:; examples/seven_guis/tests/mcp_log.rs:; the needles at examples/seven_guis/tests/common/mod.rs:); `host_log`'s runs in the state directory `hl-popup` (examples/seven_guis/tests/host_log.rs:) under `#[cfg(unix)]`, as every host-driving test there does; `mcp_log`'s records nothing and no `ml-popup` directory exists — as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-31-select-popup/report.md

- seven_guis CRUD: since 2026-10-10-snapshot-states the person rows are `option`s of a `listbox` by `role` attribute and are not focusable (examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs:; examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs: — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-10-snapshot-states/report.md); since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness the list `crud-list` takes `tabindex="0"` and an `onkeydown` — the third CRUD Tab stop — and, focused, ArrowDown selects the next visible row (the first when none is selected), ArrowUp the previous, Home the first and End the last, each setting the selection and the two fields as a row's click does, a key at the end of the list or ArrowUp with no row selected changing nothing; the tree's focus is the list, never the option — the builder reads no `aria-activedescendant`, so an assistive technology learns the current row only from its `selected` reading — recorded, not closed: an `aria-activedescendant` read in the builder, or a roving focus, is SC 4.1.2 work outside the tier-0 target, kept unread on the founder's F2 «Оставить записанным (Рекомендую)» (2026-10-14, by question dialog in the overseer session, relayed by the overseer as his chosen option label) and pinned by `accessibility_active_descendant_unread` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) (tests/blitz-tests/tests/accessibility_active_descendant_unread.rs:) (examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs:; examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs:; examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/stand_keyboard.rs:) — the operator's decision, as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness/report.md; since 2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions the list is named `People` by `aria-label` (examples/seven_guis/src/tasks/crud.rs: — as measured at escher-0.1.0/chunks/2026-10-14-stand-a11y-assertions/report.md)

- **Boundary:** Persistence (sqlite)
  - **What to validate:** SQL values
  - **How (stack-specific):** Statements bind values through `params!` placeholders (apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:; apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:; apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:; apps/browser/persistence/src/lib.rs:)
| Focus — blitz-dom default input outline | `#4D90FE` | (packages/blitz-dom/assets/default.css:; packages/blitz-dom/assets/default.css:; packages/blitz-dom/assets/default.css:) |

- `eval`/`eval_module` log but do not propagate uncaught errors (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/modules.rs:); script URL resolve or fetch failures are recorded and that script is skipped (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:)

- **blitz-shell** — accessibility is a default feature enabling accesskit, accesskit_xplat and blitz-dom/accessibility (packages/blitz-shell/Cargo.toml:); each View holds an AccessibilityState wrapping an accesskit_xplat Adapter (packages/blitz-shell/src/window.rs:; packages/blitz-shell/src/accessibility.rs:)

- An element is focusable if it holds a sub-document, or is not inert, is no disabled form control and has `tabindex >= 0` or, with no tabindex, is an `<a>`/`<area>` with `href` or a `button`, `input`, `select`, `textarea`, `frame`, `iframe` or `summary`; `disabled` counts by presence on a form control alone; HTML's focus fixup is built, so a node holding focus when it comes under `inert`, a subtree moved under an inert box included, gives focus up as the mutator flushes, no DOM `blur` or `focusout` firing. The fixup reads `is_inert()` alone, so a focused control that no longer shows, by `hidden`, `style="display:none"` or CSS alone, keeps focus and takes keys, with no panic; the limit is owned by a `CARRY:` on the entry «A11y re-read».
> NO RECORDED INTENT

- **Engine, test and tool emitters** — blitz-dom, blitz-net, blitz-html, blitz-shell, blitz-paint, blitz, blitz-vibey-script, dioxus-native, dioxus-native-dom, tests/blitz-tests, wpt/runner and the CI publish builds: each one's log sites by level, message and field, and blitz-dom's `println!` dumps.

- **The free-disk step's cure is unproven:** the step in `Stand checks repeated` ran `completed · success` on CI#41192433140, taking `/dev/root` from 86 G free to 109 G free, and is not shown to be the cure: that runner had 86 GB free before the step, CI#41190771843's failed run has no `df` line, and on that run the job alone among the `ubuntu-24.04` jobs stood on the older image `20261018.96.1`, whose free disk stays unread — as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-10-31-engine-debts/evidence/ci.md

- **Unsafe aliasing:** `Node` holds a raw `*mut NodeTree` commented "This is unsafe!!" with `unsafe impl Send` and `Sync` (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:)
- Observed absent — contrast checks in the searched s05 and s11 files, and user-preference media handling in the s11 files.

- The select model stands beside them, a direct engine change for every document, remote pages included: a focused single-choice `select` (no `multiple`), its list closed, that is no disabled form control takes a pressed `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` to the next / previous enabled option and `Home` / `End` to the first / last (with none chosen, `ArrowDown` reads as `Home` and `ArrowUp` as `End`), and a character pressed with no Ctrl, Alt or Meta as typeahead — the first enabled option whose label starts with the buffered text, compared in lower case, the buffer (`select_typeahead`) starting afresh for another select or once the document's clock has moved 1 s (`TYPEAHEAD_TIMEOUT`); Enter, and a Space with no typed text standing, opens its list (below), every other key does nothing, and a released Space does nothing more (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:). A click on a select clears the typeahead and the document's text selection and focuses it through `generate_focus_events` / `set_focus_to`, and on a single select opens its list or closes one standing; the walk's disabled gate stops a disabled select first, so it neither focuses nor acts (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/pointer.rs:). Every choice that changes the chosen option or a `multiple` select's chosen set goes through the one path `apply_select_choice`, which takes the chosen set — the `CHECKED` write, the changed set, `input` then `change`, each carrying `select_value`, and a redraw — and a choice of the chosen option fires nothing (packages/blitz-dom/src/events/keyboard.rs:). Its limits: a single select's `size` is unread, and an option of a closed single select is not clicked (a driver `click` on one is refused `covered`, under a group too). - **session-start:** `Session::start(label, boot)` takes a label of 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, checked before the caller's boot runs once on the calling thread; an invalid label is `InvalidLabel` with nothing booted. A check boots through `seven_guis::stand`, reads the held harness through `harness()` / `harness_mut()`, and runs one step and waits for quiet through `act(step) -> Result<Settled, SessionError>` — the closure runs on the held harness, the harness is settled, a load in flight waited for up to `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time, settled again every 10 ms, no time moving on the held instance) since 2026-10-20-load-wait, and an instance that did not go quiet is `NotSettled(Busy)`, one still loading at the bound `NotSettled(Loads)`, a failed load ending the wait where it would otherwise have run to `LOAD_WAIT`, `settle_waiting` unedited; the step is not rolled back, and `act` is in process: nothing it reads or returns crosses the socket. A check runs a driver call through `run(&Call) -> Result<Outcome, Refusal>`: the call is validated first and a refused one has run nothing; the id of a `click`, a `type` or a `scroll` is looked up on the screen as it reads now, and one that names no element there is refused with nothing run — `stale` when the session's record of the ids its screens have read holds it, `not-found` when not (the record: id text only, at most 4096 ids, for the session's life, read by nothing outside the crate); a `click` or a `type` on an element that cannot take it is refused with one answer, the first that holds in the order `disabled` · `off-screen` · `covered`, and a refused call leaves the snapshot and both focus readings as they were; each acting verb (`click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`) is one settled step, waiting on a load in flight as `act` does on every carrier while `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint` and `graph` run no step and wait on nothing, and returns `Outcome::Acted`, `Outcome::Advanced` or `Outcome::Scrolled` with the diff of the snapshots before and after it — `scroll` adding `in_view`, whether its element is in view after the step — `snapshot` returns `Outcome::Screen` with the screen's text, or, for a screen over the snapshot budget or a `part` asked, `Outcome::Part` with one part's text and the counts `part` and `parts`, `graph` returns `Outcome::Graphed { graph }` with the screen's `UiGraph`, and an instance that did not go quiet is a result — `settled` false with its `busy` class — not rolled back. Since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot `run` also takes `screenshot`, the seventh instance verb, its `id` optional, and returns `Outcome::Shot { width, height, png }` — a PNG of the harness's raster, the whole screen or the element's bounds cropped to the part that can be seen and rounded outward — with no diff, a shot changing nothing (`has_changes` false, focus and the next snapshot unchanged); its `id` is looked up as a `click`'s is, refused `stale` or `not-found`, a crop of no pixel is refused `off-screen`, and an app with no font it can paint text with is refused `fonts-unavailable`, the eighth cause, with nothing painted (packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:). `with_time(step)` hands the session its caller's time step, the step moving the app's own time; every session accepts `advance`, which moves the session's clock by exactly `ms` and then runs the step where one was handed, `advanced_ms` reading `ms` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18). - The load wait: `LOAD_WAIT: Duration`, 5 s of wall time, re-exported at the crate root, is how long an acting step waits for a load in flight before it returns with the load still outstanding. The crate-private `settle_waiting` settles the held harness through `Harness::settle` and, while the answer is `NotSettled { busy: Busy::Loads }`, settles again every `LOAD_POLL` (10 ms, private) until the load is answered, a failed load answering it, or `LOAD_WAIT` has passed; its last sleep is the time left, then one more settle, so a wait never answered returns at or past the bound and within one settle of it, `settled` false with `busy` `loads`, while a `render` or `layout` answer returns at once. `Session::act` and the executor's settled step settle through it, so the five acting verbs (`click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll`) wait on every carrier — in process, the socket, the command line and MCP — and `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint`, `graph` and `actions`, which run no step, wait on nothing. It reads `std::time::Instant` and sleeps, and nothing else: no `tick`, `advance_time` or time step, so no time moves on the held instance while it waits, no changed-set drain, no print and no `tracing` call — `session.rs` the one clock reader among the session, the executor, the schema, validation and the JSON writer. The `settled` field's help states the bound («a load in flight waited for up to 5 s»), and on a waited step the `command` span's `passes` is the passes of the settle that went quiet. A kept check whose app meets a load can read `settled` differently on a replay whose load lands at another time (recorded, not established); the two committed Counter checks meet no load (packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/execute.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/schema.rs:; as measured at escher-0.2.0/chunks/2026-10-20-load-wait/report.md).

The `<body onload>` attribute text is wrapped into a function source string and evaluated (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/events.rs:). JS `fetch()` and ES module imports go through the same ScriptFetcher as `<script src>` (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/state.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:), and `fetch()` URLs resolve against the document base URL (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/fetch.rs:). The React reference page states React passes Trusted Types values (`TrustedHTML` / `TrustedScriptURL`) straight through to `innerHTML` and URL-bearing attributes when enabled (examples/preact/core_dom_apis.html:)
  - **Trust boundary:** The default script fetcher supports only `file:` and `data:` URLs; any other scheme returns `UnsupportedScheme` (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/fetch.rs:). A `file:` URL loads only for a `file:` document: `document_may_load` refuses it for any other document, remote pages included, with a `FetchError`, checked by JS `fetch()`, module `import` and `<script src>` alike — a narrowing of the boundary, not a widening (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/fetch.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/runtime/fetch.rs:; packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/document.rs:). A `file:` URL is read from the local filesystem with `std::fs::read_to_string` (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/fetch.rs:). Every event object created by the runtime sets `isTrusted` to true (packages/blitz-vibey-script/src/dom/event.rs:). - A `select`'s choice is held as its options' `CHECKED` element state, so `:checked` matches the chosen option; an option created with a `selected` attribute is seeded `CHECKED` (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/element.rs:). The rules, in the crate-private `node/select.rs` cited to the WHATWG `select` element: a select's options are its `option` children and its `optgroup` children's, in tree order; an option's label is its non-empty `label` attribute, else its stripped and collapsed text, and its value its `value` attribute when present, else the text; a single-choice select is settled by HTML's selectedness setting algorithm — the last chosen option, else the first option not disabled (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/node/select.rs:). The mutator records every select whose children an entry point touches and every select entering the document — a Dioxus static template is deep-cloned, so its options never pass an append —; a `selected` write sets that option chosen and, on a single-choice select, its select's other options not, a `multiple` select's others left alone, a cleared one sets it not chosen, and `flush` settles every recorded select, firing no event (packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/mutator.rs:). - **One incremental pipeline, safe identities** — style, damage, box construction, layout and paint topology are invalidated incrementally through a single code path, over versioned node ids.
  - Incremental and non-incremental layout run the same style → damage → box construction → layout pipeline; non-incremental marks every node damaged each resolve (packages/blitz-dom/src/document.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/resolve.rs:), so the two must produce identical layouts after any sequence of mutations (tests/blitz-tests/tests/incremental_oracle.rs:)
  - Blitz runs a style pass then a separate layout pass (unlike Servo, which interleaves them), accepting it is slower because it is fast enough (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/mod.rs:); inline (Parley) layout construction is deferred to a dedicated phase so text shaping can be multithreaded (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/construct.rs:)
  - The paint tree holds topology only, built once per frame after layout for damaged subtrees; geometry is derived at use time from `final_layout()` and memoised per geometry generation so a cached list cannot paint a box where layout no longer puts it (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/paint_tree.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/paint_tree_incremental.rs:)
  - Style changes are classified into damage bits and only nodes whose subtree needs relayout have their layout caches cleared (packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/damage.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/layout/damage.rs:); state changes (hover/focus/active/disabled) set no restyle hint and invalidation is driven by element snapshots (packages/blitz-dom/src/node/node.rs:)
  - Device changes (resize, zoom, color-scheme, media type) are coalesced so the stylist device is rebuilt at most once per resolve (packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_device.rs:; packages/blitz-dom/src/stylo_device.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/device_coalescing.rs:); a viewport resize invalidates only origins whose media query results changed and elements using viewport units (tests/blitz-tests/tests/resize_restyle.rs:; tests/blitz-tests/tests/resize_restyle.rs:)

- **Driver session (escher-driver):** the crate re-exports 62 names (as measured at escher-0.3.0/chunks/2026-11-08-handler-coverage/report.md) under `#![deny(missing_docs)]` — the session's `Session`, `SessionError`, `serve`, `IDLE_EXPIRY`, `LOAD_WAIT`, `start`, `attach`, `stop`, `call`, `Hello`, `Answer` and `Started`, the 29 of the command and refusal schema (named below; `NodeFieldSpec`, `ExitStatus` and `EXIT_STATUSES` since 2026-10-12-self-description), the executor's `Outcome`, the command line's `command_line`, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface the MCP server's `serve_mcp` and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the self-description's `describe` and the recording's `Check`, `Step`, `answer_digest` and `MASKED_STAND_IN` and the replay's `Replay` and `Change` and the visual lint's `Bounds`, `Defect`, `Finding` and `Reason` and the actions read's `ActionNode` and `VerbReading` and the coverage reader's `Coverage`, `HandlerRef` and `handler_coverage` from private modules, the last from the private module `coverage`, and `Busy` and `Settled` from blitz-test-harness (packages/escher-driver/src/lib.rs:).
 `Session::start(label: &str, boot: impl FnOnce() -> Harness<DioxusDocument>) -> Result<Session, SessionError>` validates the label first — 1 to 32 bytes of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`, else `InvalidLabel` with the boot not run — then runs the caller's boot once on the calling thread and owns the harness it returns, offering `label()`, `harness()`, `harness_mut()` and `act(step: impl FnOnce(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>)) -> Result<Settled, SessionError>`, which runs the step on the held instance, settles it through the load wait (below: `Harness::settle`, the Test harness contract above, settled again while a load is in flight, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`) and maps an instance that did not go quiet onto `NotSettled(Busy)` — the step is not rolled back, and nothing `act` reads or returns crosses the socket; `with_time(self, step: impl FnMut(&mut Harness<DioxusDocument>, u32) + 'static) -> Session` returns the session carrying a caller's time step — handed the held harness and the milliseconds an `advance` asks for, it moves the app's own time and returns nothing, the session itself moving the harness's clock on every `advance` (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) — and a session started without it carries none; the session holds a label, the harness, that optional step, one private record of the ids its screens have read and the optional crate-private recording `recording_into` sets (stated with `run`, below) — no `NodeId`, no viewport, font or scheme setting, no subscriber, and it neither reads nor drains the changed set; the crate names no app and no stand type, so the boot and the time step are the caller's (packages/escher-driver/src/session.rs:).
 `serve(state_dir: &Path, session: Session, idle_expiry: Duration) -> Result<(), SessionError>` hosts one session for the life of a process: it prepares the state directory and its socket as §Occupied Resources records (a socket file no process answers on is replaced, one a process answers on is `AlreadyRunning`, a path `std` refuses as too long is `StateDirTooLong`), answers one connection at a time on the calling thread with a 2 s read and write bound each — its accept loop non-blocking, polled every 25 ms — runs a `call` request through `Session::run` and nothing else, answering with the outcome or the refusal as one line of JSON, and on `stop`, or once no request has been answered for `idle_expiry`, drops the session and removes the socket file and the directory; every answered request — a refused or malformed one included — counts toward `served` and starts the idle count again, and a connection that breaks before its request is whole does neither; `IDLE_EXPIRY`, what a command line's host serves under, is 1,800 s (packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/host.rs:).
 The lifecycle another process drives, and the call it sends: `attach(state_dir) -> Result<Hello, SessionError>` with `Hello { pid: u32, label: String, served: u64, idle_expiry_s: u64 }` — no socket file reads `NoSession`, a socket nothing answers on `Dead`, an answer outside the protocol `Protocol`; `stop(state_dir)` sends the stop request and waits, at most 5 s, until the state directory is gone (`Timeout` past it); `start(state_dir, host: std::process::Command, ready: Duration) -> Result<Started, SessionError>` with `Started { child: std::process::Child, hello: Hello }` attaches first (answered reads `AlreadyRunning`, nothing spawned), spawns `host` as configured and polls every 25 ms until the session answers, the host exits (`HostExited(code)`) or `ready` passes (`Timeout`, the host killed and reaped); it does not check that the answering pid is the child it spawned; `call(state_dir, call: &Call) -> Result<Answer, SessionError>` with `Answer { accepted: bool, json: String }` sends one call and returns its answer — it runs `validate` first, so a call the schema refuses is answered there with its refusal and reaches no session, and every call sent fits the request bound; the answer is read under a 30 s bound on each read (`Timeout` past it; pinned since 2026-10-14-quality-gates by the unix-only `client::imp::tests::an_answer_read_past_its_bound_is_a_timeout`, which reads the bound equal to `wire::ANSWER_BOUND`, 30 s, and a read past a shortened bound on a listener that never answers as `Timeout`), an `oversize` reply reads as `AnswerTooLarge` — the call ran, and what it did is not rolled back — and with no session to reach it reads as `attach` does (packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/client.rs:).
 `SessionError` is exactly `AlreadyRunning` · `NoSession` · `Dead` · `HostExited(Option<i32>)` · `Timeout` · `Protocol` · `InvalidLabel` · `StateDirTooLong` · `StateDirNotPrivate` · `Unsupported` · `Io(std::io::ErrorKind)` · `NotSettled(Busy)` · `AnswerTooLarge` · `RecordDirNotPrivate` · `RecordingFailed` — fifteen — with `Display`, `std::error::Error`, `kind() -> &'static str` (one fixed kebab-case word per variant, `already-running` through `recording-failed`), since 2026-10-12-self-description `remedy() -> &'static str`, and `to_json()`; since that chunk each variant's kind, meaning and remedy are one row of a crate-private table, `SESSION_ERRORS: [ErrorSpec; 15]` of `ErrorSpec { kind, meaning, remedy, repeats }` (`repeats` is not served), which `kind()`, `remedy()` and `Display` read; every message is a fixed string — the row's meaning, the `Io` arm appending the kind's name and the `NotSettled` arm the class's — and none carries a path, a label, an id or a value; `StateDirTooLong`'s message states its bound as a figure, at most 94 bytes as given on Linux and 90 on every other target, and its remedy is to name a shorter path for the state directory, or a relative one, which counts only its own bytes; two rows share a remedy, each later row naming the earlier — `dead` repeats `no-session`'s, `answer-too-large` repeats `not-settled`'s (packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:; packages/escher-driver/src/error.rs:).
 The wire is crate-private and versioned `v3`: one request line and one reply line per connection, `\n`-terminated — requests `hello v3`, `stop v3` and `call v3 <verb> [<name>=<kind>:<value>]…` (kinds `t` text · `n` whole number · `f` flag; the verb, the names and a text value percent-escaped byte for byte — every byte but an ASCII letter, a digit, `-`, `_`, `.` and `~` — and decoded strictly: uppercase hex only, no escape of a byte that needs none, the decoded bytes UTF-8, a number in its one spelling), at most 16,384 bytes where `v1` admitted 64, the widest call the schema admits being 15,360 bytes of values; replies `ok v3 pid={pid} label={label} served={n} idle_expiry_s={s}`, `ok v3 stopping`, `refused version` (a known word with another version) and `refused malformed` (anything else, a call the decoder does not read included), at most 128 bytes — the widest `hello` measures 122 — and, to a call, `ok v3 accepted <json>`, `ok v3 refused <json>`, `ok v3 oversize` or `ok v3 recording-failed` — sent in place of the answer when the host's recording ended after the call, the client reading it as `RecordingFailed` — an answer bounded at 1,048,576 bytes on its JSON line alone and `frame` the one function that turns an answer into its reply; `{n}` counts every request the host answered before this one, refusals included; a refusal or a broken connection changes nothing, an `oversize` reply is no refusal — the call ran and what it did stands — and a `stop` takes effect once its reply is written (packages/escher-driver/src/wire.rs:). On a non-unix target `serve`, `start`, `attach`, `stop` and — for a call the schema admits — `call` return `Unsupported`, and so does `Session::recording_into`; a `Session` held in process without a recording works on every target.

- `Session::run(&Call) -> Result<Outcome, Refusal>` — the one entry point that runs a call. `validate` first: a refused call has run nothing, and a session-level verb (`start`, `status`, `stop`) is refused `unknown-verb`. Then per verb: `snapshot` reads the screen once and dispatches nothing — with no `part` and a text of at most `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` bytes it returns `Snapshot::to_text`'s text as `Outcome::Screen`, otherwise (since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts) it cuts `text_parts(SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET)` and returns part `n` — `part`, or 1 when absent — as `Outcome::Part` with the count `parts`, a part past the last the empty text with the same `parts`; `click`, `type`, `scroll` and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a `screenshot` given an `id` look their id up on the screen as it reads NOW (the snapshot lists it, and the first `element_ids()` pair with it resolves through `get_node`) — an id that names no element there is refused with nothing run, `stale` when the session's record of ids read holds it, `not-found` when not. A `click` or a `type` on an element that cannot take it is then refused, one answer in a fixed order: `disabled` (the snapshot reads `enabled: Some(false)`), `off-screen` (the centre of its `bounds` is outside `BaseDocument::visible_region` — the viewport and every scrolling box that holds it, a row or a group of an open select list reading the list's scrollport in place of its clipping boxes; under a rotation a box's visible part reads as the bounding box of its rotated padding box, so an element in a corner it does not show can read in view, a measured limit `off-screen`'s meaning states), `covered` (the hit at that page point never reaches it, where a select list stands open a hit answering the list first, so a button under the list reads `covered`; an option of a closed single select is not clicked — a `click` on one is refused `covered`, under a group too, while a `click` on a `multiple` select's row is accepted and chooses it, a `click` on a single select opens its list or closes one standing, as `click`'s help says of a select, and a `click` on an open list's row chooses it). Otherwise they click the centre of the element's snapshot `bounds` plus the viewport's scroll, but for a `type` on a select, single or `multiple` (`Target` carries `select`), which does not click, a click landing on a `multiple` select's row at the centre and opening a single select's list: the crate-private `focus_select` focuses it with no click, so `type` fires no DOM focus events on a single select, clears the typeahead (`BaseDocument::clear_select_typeahead`, its one non-test caller), without which a second `type` joins the first's text, and closes any list (`BaseDocument::close_select_list`), and a text opening on a space types nothing on any select, since no label can match and on a `multiple` select the Space would flip a row — two `click`s on one point with no `advance` of at least 500 ms between them read as a double click, as `click`'s help says (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); `type` then replaces what the control holds — where the snapshot reads a `value` for the target (an empty text input reads one) it presses the engine's select-all (`a` with Control, Super on macOS) and types, and with an empty text deletes the selection, so an empty text clears; on a select the text is the engine's typeahead, choosing the first option whose label starts with it and, on a `multiple` select, its match alone, as `type`'s help says; `press` presses its key on what holds focus (shift when asked; it carries no Ctrl, so a set of rows of a `multiple` select that are not adjacent cannot be built through the driver, as its help states) — since 2026-10-13-stand-keyboard-harness a pressed `enter`, or a `space`, on a focused button with no `disabled` attribute dispatches its click (the engine's keyboard activation, [Scrolling and input]), and on a focused single select with its list closed a pressed `enter`, or a `space` with no typed text standing, opens its list, whose keys then move the highlight, choose and close, `press`'s help stating the keys on a closed select; `advance` moves the harness's clock by exactly its milliseconds (`Harness::advance_time`) inside one settled step on every session — the engine's animations, the overlay scrollbar fade and the app's own time together — then hands them to the session's time step where one was handed (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); `scroll` applies none of the three checks, scrolls every scrolling box that holds the element and then the viewport, at once (`Harness::scroll_into_view`), a row of an open select list writing that list's `scroll_y` alone, and answers `in_view` — false when no scroll could bring it into view or the element was removed; it is never refused for that; `screenshot` (since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) dispatches nothing and is no step — with no `id` it returns the whole screen, with an `id` it crops the frame to the part of the element's bounds that can be seen, rounded outward to whole pixels, a crop of no pixel refused `off-screen`; an app whose font context resolves no `sans-serif` family (`BaseDocument::can_paint_text` false) is refused `fonts-unavailable` with nothing painted; the frame is the harness's `screenshot`, written as a PNG by the private `image::png`, and a shot changes nothing (`has_changes` stays false, focus and the next snapshot unchanged); `lint` (since 2026-10-19-visual-lint) takes no argument and its arm calls `Session::lint`, so a lint dispatches nothing, runs no step and settles nothing, answering its findings; `graph` (since 2026-11-07-ui-graph) takes no argument — an argument refused `malformed` with nothing run — and answers `Outcome::Graphed`, the screen's graph read through the read-only `DioxusDocument::graph`, its node ids feeding the session's record of ids, so a graph read dispatches nothing, runs no step and settles nothing; `actions` (since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here) takes no argument — an argument refused `malformed` with nothing run — and its arm calls `Session::actions(&mut self) -> Vec<ActionNode>`, which reads one snapshot and one `element_ids` map, records every id it reads in the session's record of ids and, for each node `DioxusDocument::actionable_nodes` lists and each verb of the crate-private `target_verbs` (the table's `Level::Instance` rows with an `ArgKind::Id` argument, in table order, today `click` · `type` · `scroll` · `screenshot`), builds the call the crate-private `call_naming` spells (a required non-target argument a fixed in-bound value, `type`'s `text` the empty text) and runs it through `validate` and then the crate-private `check_target` — the one per-verb target check, which the four id-taking arms of `Session::execute` also call, keeping no check of their own — reading `stale` for a node that resolves to no element, so an actions read dispatches nothing, runs no step, settles nothing and changes nothing, answering `Outcome::Actions`. Each acting verb is one settled step: snapshot, step, the load wait over `Harness::settle`, snapshot, diff — so since 2026-10-20-load-wait the five acting verbs wait on a load in flight, for at most `LOAD_WAIT`, on every carrier (in process, the socket, the command line and MCP), while `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint`, `graph` and `actions`, which run no step, wait on nothing. A refused call leaves the snapshot and both focus readings as they were.

- The command span: every call handed to `Session::run` leaves one `tracing` span — target `escher_driver`, name `command`, INFO, built by hand with `tracing::info_span!` (no `#[instrument]`), entered before `validate` and held until `run` returns. Its eight fields are each created unrecorded and recorded only where they apply: `verb` (the verb table's own word, never the caller's text — a session-level verb's and, since 2026-10-12-self-description, the tool-level `help`'s too, beside `unknown-verb`), `cause` (`Cause::name()` of the returned refusal), `settled`, `busy` (the schema's busy-class word), `passes` (the settle's pass count, recorded whenever the settle answered quiet), and `added` · `removed` · `changed` (the lengths of the returned diff). `snapshot` and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, an accepted `screenshot` record `verb` alone, as do an accepted `lint`, a part read, an accepted `graph` and an accepted `actions`; a refused call `verb` and `cause` only. Never fielded: `in_view`, `advanced_ms`, the screen text or its length, a part's number, the part count, a shot's image, its size or its dimensions, a lint's findings or their count, a graph, its ids or its names, an actions answer, its ids or its verb readings, the label, the record of ids, the recording, its directory or its kept check (since 2026-10-19-session-recording), any argument, any `Command`, `Call`, `ArgValue`, `Outcome`, `Refusal` or `Fault`. The crate installs no subscriber: with none the span is disabled; under escher's sink it is one line per call at `info` or below, none at the default `warn` — an `escher-session` host writes it for every hosted call. A call the schema refuses on the command line or in `client::call` reaches no session and opens no span; an idle expiry writes no record. The command line's `coverage` role adds no span, each replayed step leaving its own `command` span through `Session::run`.

- A driver call is checked by `escher_driver::validate` — a session-level one (`start` · `status` · `stop`) or the tool-level `help` by `validate_session` — before anything runs: a closed verb table of fourteen verbs in three levels (`screenshot`, the seventh asked of the held instance, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, `lint`, the eighth, since 2026-10-19-visual-lint: no argument, one result field `findings`, running no step, and `graph`, the ninth, since 2026-11-07-ui-graph: no argument, any argument refused `malformed` with nothing run, result fields `nodes` and `states`, running no step — a ratified boundary widening onto every ratified carrier, and `actions`, the tenth, since 2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here: no argument, any argument refused `malformed` with nothing run, one result field `nodes`, running no step — a ratified boundary widening onto every ratified carrier, the `keyed` field PROVISIONAL), seven argument kinds with bounds (`part`, the seventh since 2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts, `snapshot`'s one optional argument, a whole number from 1 to 1000, `MAX_PART`), one fixed refusal order, no panic path on what a call supplies, and no `Session` in its signature — so a refused call changes nothing. A refusal is one of eight causes with fixed texts (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18; `fonts-unavailable` since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot) and holds nothing of the call; keep it that way (no id, name, value or call-supplied argument name in a `Refusal`, a `Fault`, a test name or an assertion message). The schema is executed by `escher_driver::Session::run`, which validates first, and since 2026-10-10-driver-cli it is reached from outside the process by three surfaces, each through `validate` before anything is sent or run: the socket's `call` request, which a host runs through `Session::run` and nothing else, since 2026-10-10-mcp-surface an MCP `tools/call`, whose arguments of the wrong JSON kind are refused `malformed` before the server runs it through `Session::run` (session verbs through `validate_session`), and the `escher-session` command line (`escher_driver::command_line`) — a closed argv reader whose usage line, refusals and session errors write back nothing the caller typed, and whose stdout is the command's answer (ids, names, values and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a shot's base64 PNG and a lint's findings by the ratified crossing), never a log line; an acting driver command waits on a load in flight for at most `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time, re-settling every 10 ms, moving no time on the held instance, then `settled: false` with its busy class; since 2026-10-20-load-wait), and `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint`, `graph` and `actions` wait on none. After `validate` the executor refuses with nothing run and the instance unchanged — an id the screen does not read as `stale` or `not-found`, a `click` or a `type` on a target that cannot take it as `disabled`, `off-screen` or `covered`, in that order; a `screenshot` of an app with no font it can paint text with as `fonts-unavailable` before anything is painted, and a `lint` of one before anything is read, and one whose crop to the visible part of its element's bounds holds no pixel as `off-screen`, every refused shot leaving the instance unchanged. An `Outcome` holds ids, names and values and, since 2026-10-12-headless-screenshot, a shot's PNG bytes (`Outcome::Shot`) and a lint's findings (`Outcome::Linted { findings }`: stable ids, closed defect words and numbers only) and a screen's part (`Outcome::Part { text, part, parts }`, the snapshot text's own lines, written `{"text":…,"part":n,"parts":m}`) and a UI graph (`Outcome::Graphed { graph: UiGraph }`, written `{"nodes":[…],"states":[…]}`, its node ids also feeding the session's record of ids) and an actions answer (`Outcome::Actions { nodes }`, written `{"nodes":[…]}`: ids, owner ids, `keyed` booleans, verb words and closed cause words), prints them under `Debug` and is written as JSON by `to_json` alone — as a command's answer, or as an MCP tool result's text — never log or field one.
